about.title: Every era leaves a trace. Here is ours.
about.lead: Pixel World is a worldwide collective archive of our time: a map of the world on which anyone can leave a creation, a memory, a passion, for the people who will come after us.

why.title: Why
why.text: Humanity has always looked for a way to leave a trace of its passage: paintings on cave walls, hieroglyphs carved in stone, manuscripts, books, photographs. Every era found its own way of handing its story down. Ours is made of conversations that fade, photos that sleep in phones and websites that disappear: little of what we live every day is kept in a form that someone could read in a hundred years. Here, each trace is chosen, with a title, an author, a date and a place, and together they make a readable fragment of our era. Today, it is Pixel World's turn.

how.title: How it works
how.text: You choose a rectangle on the map, you create your trace in the editor (an image, a drawing, a text), you give it a title, a category and, if you want, the place it is about. After a quick look by the moderators, it has a page of its own, that you can share, and you can invite other people to draw on it with you.

time.title: A time to tell it
time.text: The founding edition lasts 365 days: this is the time left to take part. When it closes, nothing can be bought or changed any more: the edition becomes a historical archive, kept as it was and open to everybody. The opening and the closing are decided by us, announced, and enforced by the server, never by a browser.

It is not real estate, nor an intellectual property right, and it is not a promise that the archive will be kept for ever: the terms say exactly what is promised.

rules.title: Community rules
rules.intro: Pixel World is a collective archive that everybody can see. These rules keep it a place people enjoy visiting. They apply to every image, text and link published on the map.

p: Drawings, pixel art, photographs, logos, messages, symbols and collective creations are welcome, as long as you have the right to use them and they respect the rules below.

ul: Hateful, discriminatory or harassing content, including symbols of hate groups.
Sexual or pornographic content, and any sexual content involving minors (reported to the authorities).
Graphic violence, gore, or content that encourages self-harm or dangerous acts.
Scams, phishing, fake giveaways, malware or links to such content.
Illegal or misleading advertising, and promotion of illegal goods or services.
Content that infringes copyright, trademarks or other rights: only publish what you created or are allowed to use.
Personal data about other people, doxxing, or impersonation of a person or organisation.
Anything that is illegal in the country of the operator or of the person who published it.

p: Commercial announcements are allowed when they are legal and truthful, and they must be identifiable: tick “This creation is an advertisement” when you publish. Advertisements are labelled as such, and their links are marked as sponsored.

Links must start with https and lead to a site you are allowed to promote. They are shown with their domain, open in a new tab and are marked nofollow. We may remove any link that leads to a harmful or deceptive destination.

Every new creation, and every modification, is reviewed before it is displayed. We cannot promise that an image will be accepted. If a creation is refused you can submit another one for the same parcel.

Anyone signed in can report a creation with the “Report” button. Reports are reviewed by moderators, and we keep the information needed to handle a report (what was displayed, when, and who published it) for as long as the law requires or permits.
Depending on the seriousness, we may refuse or hide a creation, remove a parcel, or suspend an account. Moderation decisions are recorded in an internal log. You can contact us to contest a decision.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of Pixel World and the payment you make to leave a trace on its map. They are a provisional text, written for the launch: it must be reviewed and completed by the operator's legal counsel before the public launch.

p: Pixel World is operated by {operatorName}, {operatorAddress}. Registration: {operatorRegistration}. VAT number: {operatorVat}. Contact: {operatorEmail}.

Pixel World is a collective archive of our time. It is drawn on a virtual grid of 1,000,000,000 pixels (40,000 × 25,000). A parcel is a rectangle of at least 25 pixels. Your payment is a contribution to this collaborative work; in return you get a digital right to use that rectangle, according to these terms, to display one creation on it.

A parcel is a virtual placement on a digital map. It is not real estate, nor a geographic, territorial or intellectual property right, and it gives you no right over the places the map depicts. Nor is it a promise that the archive will be kept for ever: see “How long a trace lasts” below.

Land and water are for sale, as two separate categories. A land parcel covers the land pixels of its rectangle: it may include some sea along a coast, but at least half of its pixels must be land (the exact share is set by the administrators). A water parcel covers the water pixels of its rectangle: it may include some land along a coast, but at least half of its pixels must be water. You pay for the pixels your parcel covers only: the pixels of your rectangle that belong to the other category are cut away and offered, or discounted if a reduced price is in force, and the order summary shows the split before you pay. A land parcel and a water parcel may share the same rectangle, since they never share a pixel. Whatever you create on a water parcel is shown in three tints of blue. The counters on the map count the pixels covered by parcels, land and water.

The initial price is €0.25 per pixel for buyers in the euro area and $0.25 per pixel for buyers elsewhere, charged in the currency of the buyer's country as detected when the order is placed, calculated automatically from the number of pixels and always recomputed on our servers. We may change the price for future sales; parcels already bought are not affected. Payments are processed by Stripe; we never see or store your card number.

When you start a purchase the pixels are reserved for you for a limited time. If you do not pay within that time the reservation is released. Your parcel is attributed only when the payment provider has confirmed the payment to us.
The amount to pay is always shown, in full, before you confirm the payment.

A group project lets several people pay together for one parcel. Its creator designs the parcel and sends it to moderation; once it is accepted, the zone is reserved for the duration the creator chose (7, 14 or 30 days) and anybody with an account may contribute, from the minimum amount shown on the project page.

A contribution is paid through the same payment provider as a purchase, in the currency of the project. The contributions to a project can never exceed the price of its parcel. If the goal is reached before the end, the parcel becomes the creator's, as if they had bought it, and the contributions are kept as the payment for it. If the goal is not reached by the end, or if the creator withdraws the project, every contribution is refunded automatically to the payment method that was used. Contributions are not displayed publicly: only the total and the number of contributors are shown.

A contributor receives no ownership, share or right over the parcel. The creator alone holds the digital right to use the parcel and is alone responsible for its content, which is reviewed by moderators like any other creation. [To be reviewed by a lawyer: the holding of funds between a contribution and the end of the project, the right of withdrawal, who issues the invoice, the VAT on each contribution, and the information to give before payment.]
Taxes, where applicable, are calculated and shown at checkout. [Tax treatment, invoicing details and consumer withdrawal or refund rules: to be defined by the operator with legal counsel.]

You keep your rights on what you publish and you guarantee that you are allowed to publish it. You grant Pixel World a worldwide, non-exclusive licence to display, reproduce and promote your creation on the site, in share previews and in material that presents the project.

Your creation is archived on a public page of its own, with its title, the username of its author, its category, the place it is about (if you gave one) and the date it was archived. The place is a text you choose (and, optionally, a country): never exact coordinates.
Creations are published after moderation and may be refused, hidden or removed if they break the community rules or the law.

The archive is organised in editions. The founding edition lasts 365 days from the day the operator opens it. The opening and the closing are decided by the operator, announced on the site, and enforced by the server, never by a browser.

When an edition closes, nothing can be bought any more and its creations are frozen: they stay readable and the map can still be explored, but their authors can no longer change them. Moderators keep the power to hide or remove a creation that breaks the rules or the law, even after the closing; the removal is recorded. A payment already started when the edition closes has a short delay to complete; one that would complete after it is refunded.
[To be reviewed by a lawyer: the closing date as a term of the contract, and what happens to a purchase made shortly before it.]

A trace stays attributed to you, and on the map, for as long as the service operates and these terms are respected. We want the archive to stay readable for a long time, but we do not promise that it will be kept for ever. [Minimum duration, notice period if the service ends, preservation of the archive after the end, and transfer rules: to be defined by the operator with legal counsel.]
You are responsible for your account. We may suspend an account that breaks these terms or the community rules.
The service is provided as is. [Limitation of liability and governing law: to be defined by the operator with legal counsel.]

credits.title: Credits & licences
credits.intro: Pixel World stands on open data and open-source software. Thank you to everyone who made them.

ul: Land, country and administrative (département, state, province) outlines: Natural Earth (public domain), 1:110m, 1:50m and 1:10m scales; land and countries are distributed through the world-atlas package (ISC).
French commune boundaries (about 35,000 towns and villages): Etalab "contours des communes", Licence Ouverte 2.0, simplified and distributed by the open repository gregoiredavid/france-geojson.

City names and positions: GeoNames (geonames.org), licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, distributed through the all-the-cities package (MIT). Cities of 1,000 inhabitants and more are shown as you zoom in.

p: The map uses the Web Mercator projection (the one of every online map) on a grid of 40,000 × 25,000 pixels, from 56.7°S to 83.8°N (all of Greenland and Tierra del Fuego included). The map wraps around horizontally: its edge is in the Bering Strait, so Russia's far east continues into Alaska when you pan, and no country is cut or drawn twice. A pixel is about 1 km wide at the equator and gets smaller towards the poles, like on any Mercator map; the vertical scale is fitted to the frame, about 5% below a pure Mercator. The level of detail (borders, départements, commune boundaries, cities) increases as you zoom.
Bricolage Grotesque, Instrument Sans and Jersey 10, all under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
Built with Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Stripe, sharp and many other open-source projects.

edition.title: The edition (the 365 days)
edition.lead: The state of the edition is decided by the database, from its own clock. The 365 days only start when an administrator opens the edition here: nothing else (no deployment, no setting) can start them. Every action below is written to the audit log.
edition.unavailable: The edition cannot be read: the database is probably missing the latest migration (run node scripts/migrate.mjs).

explain.prelaunch: No date, nothing is for sale. The map can be visited. The 365 days have not started.
explain.open: Purchases, group projects and creations are open until the closing date.
explain.settling: Nothing can be bought any more. The payments that were already under way can still finish, and their buyers can still send their creation, until the end of the reservation delay. Then the creations freeze and the snapshot is taken.
explain.closed: Nothing can be bought, no creation can be changed. The archive can be visited. Moderators can still take things down.

edition.confirmLabel: To confirm, type the name of the edition: {name}

open.title: Open the edition
open.help: The {n} days start at the moment you click. This cannot be undone from here (only a rehearsal on a site that sold nothing can go back to pre-launch).

extend.title: Postpone the closing
extend.help: The closing can only be moved later, never brought forward, and never beyond twice the length of the edition after the opening. It is recorded in the audit log with your note.

close.title: Close the sales now
close.help: Purchases and projects stop at once. The payments under way can finish during the reservation delay; then everything freezes and the snapshot is taken.

reset.help: "Back to pre-launch" is for a rehearsal: it is refused as soon as a parcel is reserved or bought, or a payment was made.

snap.title: New snapshot
snap.help: A snapshot is never rewritten. After a takedown, or a creation that moderation approved late, take a new one: it becomes the next revision.

edition.adminOnly: Only administrators can change the edition.

errors.px_edition_bad_state: Not possible in the current state of the edition.

errors.px_edition_not_empty: Refused: a parcel is reserved or bought, or a payment was made. Only an empty site can go back to pre-launch.

ranking.title: Ranking
ranking.lead: The most liked creations and creators of Pixel World.
ranking.empty: Nobody has been liked in this period yet.
ranking.rules: Only likes from other, active accounts count: the author's own like on their creation, and likes from suspended accounts, are ignored. A creation that is hidden by moderation is not ranked. Ties share a rank; the earlier creation comes first. The creators' score is the sum of the likes of all their creations.
